High level: Nimble is comfortable with a 3-year committed prepay in exchange for the term discount you quoted, but our CFO prefers to see invoices split by fiscal year for budgeting purposes (Year 1 = FY26 partial, Year 2 = FY27, Year 3 = FY28).

Questions we have:
- Can Redwood issue separate invoices aligned to our fiscal years while keeping a single prepay contract?
- Will that split change the discount structure or the effective price (e.g., does the term discount apply to the total or to each invoice separately)?
- For audit: what documentation will you provide so our accounting team can justify deferring/recognizing revenue (e.g., SOW with explicit payment schedule + confirmation of service commencement dates)?

We attached a draft SOW and our preferred payment schedule (simple split). Can you loop in finance and confirm?

Thanks — I can do a quick 15-min call if needed.

—Ethan

Ethan — great to meet you last week. I ran a quick options matrix with Marcus and attached a suggested payment schedule (nimble_payment_schedule_v1.xlsx) plus our SLA-credit matrix. Summary proposal: 

Option A (preferred, lowest admin):
- Invoice 1 (upon signature): 60% of total committed value (covers Year 1 + initial runway)
- Invoice 2 (12 months after signature): 20%
- Invoice 3 (24 months after signature): 20%
- Term discount is applied to the total committed amount up front (so the numbers in the spreadsheet reflect discounted amounts).

Option B (fiscal-year-aligned; matches your ask):
- Invoice 1 (pro-rated to FY26): X% (covers signature date -> 2026-12-31)
- Invoice 2 (calendar FY27): Y%
- Invoice 3 (calendar FY28): Z%
- We can map the percentages so the total equals the contracted discounted value; see sheet tab 'FY-split'.

SLA crediting: we will include an SLA crediting clause in the SOW that: (a) defines the credit as a refund/credit to future invoices; (b) outlines how credits are applied if invoice already settled; and (c) includes a simple example for auditors. The SLA-credit-matrix.xlsx shows how credits are capped per month and per year.

Next step: Marcus — would you add the accounting language we should include in the SOW (deferred revenue wording + suggested invoice descriptions for Nimble's GL)? Once we have wording I'll update the SOW and route to your legal.

Thanks,

Ethan / Marissa / Irene — quick finance take and recommended contract language for auditors. High level: we need (1) a clear payment schedule in the SOW, (2) a statement that the customer has a non-cancellable commitment to the total amount (so revenue can be deferred and recognized over the service period under ASC 606), and (3) invoice descriptions that tie each invoice to the same commitment ID so your accounting can map cash to the liability.

Suggested accounting text to include in the SOW (for your auditors):
"Redwood Inference shall invoice the Customer according to the payment schedule set forth in Exhibit A. The Customer's payments represent a multi-year prepayment for Redwood's cloud inference services. Upon receipt, Redwood will record the payments as deferred revenue and recognize revenue ratably over the service period specified in the SOW unless otherwise specified in Exhibit A. Each invoice will include the Master Commitment ID and an invoice-level reference to the portion of the commitment being collected. SLA credits, if any, will be posted as contra-revenue and applied to future invoices or refunded per the mutual agreement in Section 5."

Invoice mechanics practicalities:
- Split invoicing (Option B) is fine — it does not change the total discount so long as the SOW shows the total contracted discounted value.
- For FY-aligned invoices we suggest adding a one-line invoice description like: "Prepay commitment DEAL-9743 — FY27 allocation (portion of total committed value)." That makes it straightforward for Nimble to match cash receipts to liability amortization.
- We can provide a short 'letter for auditors' confirming this approach once contracts are signed; that letter will include the same language above and sample amortization schedule.

Actions I'm taking:
1) I'll draft the SOW paragraph and a short auditor confirmation note (will upload to the Drive link).
2) I confirm we can issue three invoices per the FY-aligned splits.
3) We will mark SLA credits as contra-revenue; if Nimble prefers credits as refunds instead, that affects cash flow but not recognition theory — let us know preference.

Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
